Citation.description: One passage an answer drew on, numbered as the answer numbers it.

n.description: the number in the answer's text: [1], [2]

name.description: the source's file name, as source_list names it

url.description: where the source was read from; empty for a note or a research report

topic.description: what to research, in plain words

Source.description: One source that is part of a collection.

name.description: the stored file name; pass it to source_remove

url.description: where it was read from; empty for a pasted note or a research report

data_base64.description: the file's bytes in standard base64; at most 25 MB before encoding

name.description: the file's name with its extension, which picks how it is read: pdf, docx, pptx, xlsx, md, markdown, txt or csv

SourceAddResult.description: The outcome of reading one page or keeping one note.

chars.description: readable text kept; a few hundred means a thin page

error.description: why it was NOT added (unreadable, blocked, refused); empty when ok

ok.description: true when it was added as a source

url.description: the page asked for; empty for a note or a file

text.description: the note itself, in plain text or Markdown; at least a paragraph

title.description: a name for it; the first words of the text when absent

urls.description: up to 8 http(s) links; each is opened in a real browser and read

results.description: one per url, in order, failures included

sources.description: source names from source_list; every source when absent

answer.description: Markdown, with [n] markers after the claims

citations.description: only the ones the answer cites, in order of first use

url.description: pass the best ones to source_add_urls

info.description: Gather the material a collection's decks, audio overviews, mind maps and notes are made from: search the web, add pages, notes or files, check what is there, and ask what it says.
info.title: SourcesService

methods.description: Start a new, untitled collection to collect sources in (the same as collection_create with no title). Returns its cid: pass it as sid to every source_* call, and as collection to session_build.
methods.name: draft_create

methods.description: Read web pages into a collection as sources. Each result says whether that page was added and, if not, why; replace a failed page with another search result.
methods.name: source_add_urls

methods.description: Add a pasted note or any text you already have to a collection as a source.
methods.name: source_add_text

methods.description: Add a document to a collection as a source: PDF, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Markdown, text or CSV, sent as base64. It is read into text and titled by its file name; the result says why when it could not be read.
methods.name: source_add_file

methods.description: List the sources in a collection, to check what its outputs will be made from.
methods.name: source_list

methods.description: Remove one source from a collection by its name; false when there was no such source.
methods.name: source_remove

methods.description: Search the web and return result pages (title, url, snippet). Nothing is added: pass the best urls to source_add_urls.
methods.name: web_search

methods.description: Research a broad topic in depth (reads many pages; about a minute at Quick depth, a few at Standard, per the Web research depth setting) and add the written report to a collection as one source.
methods.name: deep_research

methods.description: Answer a question from a collection's sources, citing the passages each claim rests on. Use it whenever the person asks what their material says.
methods.name: source_ask
